title: Holistic dequant suppression prefetcher for mixed-precision prefill
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Mixed-precision execution (INT8/FP8 fastpaths) delivers strong throughput but introduces dynamic dequantization overheads during prefill and decode that amplify tail latency for short queries and streaming workloads. Our current prefill scheduler indiscriminately triggers kernel handoffs and per-token dequant casts which cause small but frequent stalls and increased GPU <-> host synchronization.

Goal: Implement a holistic Dequant Suppression Prefetcher (DSP) that proactively gates dequant operations and schedules kernel handoffs in a token- and subword-aware manner to reduce stall count and SLO tail latency while preserving correctness and model output fidelity. The DSP should be compatible with hosted, dedicated, and private runtimes and be configurable per-customer/model via runtime flags.
background_context: Existing telemetry (runtime-1.18 perf dashboard) shows 5-12% tail latency regressions for 1-16 token inputs on mixed-precision models when a format switch (INT8 <-> FP8) occurs during prefill. Related engineering tickets cover quantization-aware scheduling heuristics (ENG-561234, ENG-42817) and token-adaptive budgeters; this work unifies those ideas into a single prefetching/gating layer. Key constraints: must avoid correctness regressions for models sensitive to numeric drift and must not increase steady-state throughput for long-sequence workloads.
acceptance_criteria: DSP implemented as a scheduling layer in the prefill path that can be toggled via runtime config
End-to-end benchmarks showing >=8% reduction in 99th-percentile prefill latency on mixed-precision models for 1-32 token requests on p4d and a100 clusters
Automatic fallback to safe dequant path on any detected numerical anomaly (per-eval guard) with telemetry event logged
Unit and integration tests covering: subword-aware gating, token-history caching, KV-hint propagation, and kernel handshake scenarios
Canary rollout plan documented and a small production canary (5% traffic) executed with no regression in model quality or error rates
out_of_scope: Model retraining or post-quantization calibration; deep changes to model weight layouts or quantization formats. This ticket focuses on runtime scheduling and kernel handshake logic only.
implementation_notes:
Proposed algorithm: 1) Track per-request recent-format-stability score using token and subword boundaries; 2) If stability score above threshold, suppress per-token dequant and request a batched dequant only at safe boundaries (e.g., end-of-subword or punctuation); 3) Use KV-cache hinting to align upcoming prefill work to an intended precision fastpath; 4) If the scheduler detects imminent format switch due to a heavy-precision token, schedule a lightweight asynchronous prefetch that prepares the alternate kernel without blocking the decode loop.

Engineering tasks: prototype DSP in runtime scheduler, add microbench harness for kernel-handshake latencies, add telemetry events (dsp.suppressed, dsp.prefetch_started, dsp.fallback_triggered), design config knobs (suppression_threshold, lookahead_tokens, prefetch_window_ms).
tradeoffs: Aggressive suppression reduces stalls but risks numerical drift for borderline tokens; conservative thresholds preserve accuracy but yield less tail improvement. We will ship conservative defaults and expose knobs for power users. Asynchronous prefetching uses some GPU memory and scheduling slots which could slightly reduce overall throughput under extreme contention; the DSP should detect contention and back off.
risks_mitigation: Risk: silent output regression. Mitigation: guarded rollout with automatic quality checks on representative prompt sets; immediate rollback on regression. Risk: increased GPU memory pressure. Mitigation: cap prefetch buffer sizes per-worker. Risk: complexity of kernel APIs across vendor backends. Mitigation: keep kernel handshake API minimal and maintain per-backend adapter tests.
test_plan: Microbench: isolated kernel handshake latency across INT8/FP8/FP16 paths
End-to-end perf: 1-32 token P99 latency on p4d/a100 using standard prompt corpus
Correctness: run fidelity evals on existing regression prompt sets; compare logits/topk distribution after suppression vs baseline
Chaos test: force alternating precision requests and validate safe fallback triggers
Canary: 5% traffic on runtime-1.20 with continuous monitoring for 72 hours
updates: 2026-02-15: Kickoff meeting — aligned on goals and success metrics. Decided to scope first iteration to single-model fastpath (Llama-derivative) to reduce kernel adapter surface.

2026-02-23: Prototype scheduling hook submitted (RFC) for review: added suppression_threshold and lookahead_tokens knobs. Initial microbench shows a 6% P99 improvement on A100 emulation with suppression=0.7.

2026-03-01: Design review notes: PM requested safer defaults; Research suggested an additional 'subword_boundary_bias' to improve suppression accuracy on tokenized languages with many subwords. Action: add bias and telemetry event for suppressed_boundaries.

2026-03-09: Integration work in progress — added KV-hint propagation to the RPC header and implemented async prefetch placeholder. Running cross-backend unit tests; one vendor adapter failing float-compare on a low-precision corner case (investigating).

2026-03-12: Benchmarked on a100 cluster: 99th improved by 9.3% for 1-8 token requests; flagged a steady-state 1.7% throughput drop under 512-batch synthetic load when prefetch_window_ms set high. Decided to implement contention-aware backoff.
